stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Design, an AI Visual Tool That Sent Figma Stock Down 7%

key_facts.fact: Claude Design is an experimental product powered by Claude Opus 4.7 that lets users create prototypes, slides, wireframes, and one-pagers through conversational prompts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced on Friday that it's launching Claude Design, a new experimental product that lets users create visuals like prototypes, slides, one-pagers, and more using Claude.

key_facts.fact: Claude Design is rolling out in research preview to Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscribers at no additional cost within existing limits.
key_facts.excerpt: Built on Claude Opus 4.7, the feature is available via the palette icon in the left-hand navigation panel of Claude.ai for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscribers.

key_facts.fact: Usage of Claude Design is tracked separately from standard Claude chat and Claude Code limits, with individual weekly allowances.
key_facts.excerpt: Usage of Claude Design is tracked separately from the standard Claude chat and Claude Code limits. Subscribers have individual weekly allowances that sit alongside existing limits rather than replacing them.

key_facts.fact: The tool reads a team's codebase and design files during onboarding to extract design systems (colors, typography, components) and applies them automatically to every project.
key_facts.excerpt: During onboarding, Claude will read a team's codebase and design files to extract colors, typography, and components, then apply that system automatically to every subsequent project.

key_facts.fact: Designs can be exported as ZIP, PDF, or PPTX, sent to Canva, or handed off to Claude Code for implementation with a single instruction.
key_facts.excerpt: Designs can be sent to Canva, downloaded as PDF, PPTX, or standalone HTML, saved as a folder, or shared internally. When a design is ready to ship, Claude can bundle the design intent and assets into a package that can be passed to Claude Code.

key_facts.fact: Figma's stock closed down 6.84% on Friday following the Claude Design announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Figma's shares dropped 6.84% following Claude Design's announcement on 17 April 2026.

stories.headline: Recursive Superintelligence Raises $500M+ at $4B Valuation for Self-Teaching AI

key_facts.fact: Recursive Superintelligence, a four-month-old startup, raised at least $500M in a round led by Google's venture arm GV with backing from Nvidia, at a $4B pre-money valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Recursive Superintelligence, the four-month-old AI startup founded by former Salesforce chief scientist Richard Socher, has raised at least $500 million in a round led by Google's venture arm GV with backing from chipmaker Nvidia. The financing values the London-incorporated company at $4 billion before new capital.

key_facts.fact: The round was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion, according to people familiar with the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: The round was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion, people familiar with the deal told the FT.

key_facts.fact: Co-founders include Richard Socher (ex-Salesforce chief scientist), Tim Rocktäschel (UCL professor, ex-DeepMind director), and former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi.
key_facts.excerpt: The FT named Recursive's core founders for the first time. Alongside Socher: Tim Rocktäschel, Berlin-born UCL professor and until recently director and principal scientist at Google DeepMind's Open-Endedness group. Former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi round out the publicly identified lineup.

key_facts.fact: The company aims to automate the entire AI development pipeline — from evaluation through research direction — and has about 20 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked which slice of frontier AI development Recursive wants to automate, whether evaluation, data selection, training, post-training, or research direction itself, Socher answered: 'Option C, all of the above.' About 20 people work there.

key_facts.fact: The public launch is expected around mid-May 2026, when the technical claims about self-improving AI will face their first real test.
key_facts.excerpt: The public launch is expected in May, Socher told Implicator.ai, and that is when the technical claims about self-improving AI meet the first real test.

stories.headline: OpenAI Loses Three Executives as It Sheds 'Side Quests' to Focus on Enterprise AI

key_facts.fact: Kevin Weil (VP of AI for Science, former CPO), Bill Peebles (Sora team lead), and Srinivas Narayanan (CTO of B2B Applications) all announced their departures on Friday.
key_facts.excerpt: Kevin Weil, who led the company's science research initiative, and Bill Peebles, the researcher behind AI video tool Sora, both announced their departures on Friday.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is shuttering Prism, the AI workspace for scientists Weil headed, and folding its capabilities into the Codex desktop app.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's Prism, a recently-announced research-focused 'workspace for scientists' that Weil was heading up, is being sunsetted, and OpenAI's plan is to fold its capabilities into the Codex desktop app, according to Wired.

key_facts.fact: The departures follow OpenAI shutting down Sora last month, which was losing an estimated $1 million per day in compute costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Sora, which was losing an estimated $1 million per day in compute costs, was shut down last month.

key_facts.fact: Weil's departure came one day after his team released GPT-Rosalind, a new model for life sciences and drug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: Weil's departure comes a day after his team released GPT-Rosalind, a new model to accelerate life sciences research and drug discovery.

key_facts.fact: The exits come weeks after product and business chief Fidji Simo took medical leave, marketing chief Kate Rouch stepped down, and COO Brad Lightcap moved to 'special projects.'
key_facts.excerpt: Their exits come just weeks after Fidji Simo, OpenAI's product and business chief, announced she would take a medical leave. Kate Rouch, OpenAI's marketing chief, also decided to step down to focus on her cancer recovery earlier this month, and Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's operating chief, transitioned to a new role focused on 'special projects.'

stories.headline: Amodei Meets Wiles and Bessent at White House in First Thaw Since Pentagon Blacklisting

key_facts.fact: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday to discuss Mythos and potential collaboration.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined a meeting on Friday between White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, sources briefed on the meeting told Axios.

key_facts.fact: The White House called the meeting 'productive and constructive,' saying they discussed collaboration on cybersecurity, innovation, and AI safety.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House said the 'introductory meeting' with the company was 'both productive and constructive.' 'We discussed opportunities for collaboration, as well as shared approaches and protocols to address the challenges associated with scaling this technology.'

key_facts.fact: Both sides sought to wall off the Pentagon supply-chain-risk fight from how the rest of the government engages with Anthropic, with next steps focused on giving other departments access to Mythos.
key_facts.excerpt: Going into the meeting, both sides sought to wall off the Pentagon fight from the way the rest of the government engaged with Anthropic, and next steps are expected to be about how other departments engage with Anthropic's new Mythos Preview model.

key_facts.fact: Treasury and other agencies have expressed interest in joining the list of organizations with access to Mythos, and a deal could be struck soon.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury and other government agencies have expressed interest in joining that list. Two sources told Axios prior to the White House meeting that a deal along those lines could be struck soon.

key_facts.fact: When asked about the meeting, President Trump responded 'Who?' and said he had 'no idea' Amodei was there.
key_facts.excerpt: When President Donald Trump was asked about Amodei's visit on a runway in Phoenix, Ariz., he responded, 'Who?' and then said he had 'no idea.'

key_facts.fact: The meeting comes two months after Trump blacklisted Anthropic, calling it a 'radical left, woke company' and declaring 'we will not do business with them again.'
key_facts.excerpt: The meeting comes two months after the White House derided the firm as a 'radical left, woke company'.

stories.headline: Cerebras Files for Nasdaq IPO, Reports $510M in 2025 Revenue and First-Ever Profit

key_facts.fact: Cerebras filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the SEC on Friday for a proposed IPO on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker 'CBRS.'
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras Systems Inc. today announced that it has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission relating to a proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras reported 2025 revenue of $510 million, up 76% from $290.3 million in 2024, and net income of $87.9 million, swinging from a $484.8 million net loss a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: The company had net income of $87.9 million on revenue of $510 million for 2025, compared with a net loss of $484.8 million on revenue of $290.3 million a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: This is Cerebras' second IPO attempt after withdrawing a previous filing in October following a U.S. national security review of UAE-based G42's minority investment.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the company's second attempt to list after it withdrew a previous IPO filing in October, days after a more than $1 billion fundraise that valued it at about $8 billion.

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays, and UBS Investment Bank are lead book-running managers for the offering.
key_facts.excerpt: Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays, and UBS Investment Bank will act as lead book-running managers for the proposed offering.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras is focused on inference and has tied much of its growth to OpenAI, including a $20 billion multi-year deal under which OpenAI will deploy 750 megawatts of Cerebras chips.
key_facts.excerpt: It is focused on inference and has tied much of its growth to OpenAI, including a $20 billion multi-year deal under which the ChatGPT creator will deploy 750 megawatts of Cerebras chips.

stories.headline: Cursor in Talks to Raise $2B at $50B Valuation, Nearly Doubling in Six Months

key_facts.fact: AI coding startup Cursor is nearing a raise of at least $2 billion at a $50 billion pre-money valuation, with returning investors Thrive and a16z expected to co-lead.
key_facts.excerpt: AI coding startup Cursor is nearing new funding in which the four-year-old company would raise at least $2 billion in fresh capital. Returning investors Thrive and Andreessen Horowitz are expected to lead the financing at a $50 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: The financing would nearly double Cursor's previous $29.3 billion post-money valuation from six months ago; Battery Ventures and Nvidia are also expected to participate.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing, if completed, would nearly double Cursor's previous $29.3 billion post-money valuation. Battery Ventures, a new investor, may also participate. Strategic investor Nvidia is also expected to write a check.

key_facts.fact: Cursor forecasts ending 2026 with an annualized revenue run rate of more than $6 billion, implying roughly a tripling from its $2 billion ARR in February.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor forecasts ending 2026 with an annualized revenue run rate of more than $6 billion. In February, Cursor reached $2 billion in annualized revenue.

key_facts.fact: Cursor has reached positive gross margins on enterprise sales but continues to lose money on individual developer accounts.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has reached positive gross margins on its sales to large enterprises, but continues to lose money on individual developer accounts.

key_facts.fact: A proprietary Composer model launched last November, plus use of cheaper models like Kimi, helped Cursor achieve slight overall gross margin profitability.
key_facts.excerpt: The introduction of a proprietary Composer model last November, along with the ability to call on less expensive models like China's Kimi, has helped the company achieve slight gross margin profitability.

stories.headline: FT: Anthropic Delays Wider Mythos Release Due to Compute Constraints, Not Just Safety

key_facts.fact: Multiple people with knowledge of Anthropic's operations told the FT the company is holding off from a wider Mythos release because it cannot reliably serve the model to customers, not primarily due to safety concerns.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has been limiting how widely its Mythos model is released, with sources pointing to reliability and capacity concerns as the driver. The reported issue is that Anthropic has suffered outages in recent weeks.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has suffered multiple outages in recent weeks, with March 2026 uptime dipping to 98.21% for Claude.ai, 98.32% for the API, and 98.56% for Claude Code.
key_facts.excerpt: March 2026 uptime dipped to 98.21% for Claude.ai, 98.32% for the API, and 98.56% for Claude Code. Anthropic's March 26–27 postmortem explicitly attributed elevated error rates on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 to 'networking performance degradation within our infrastructure.'

key_facts.fact: The reliability issues are shaping the Mythos rollout timeline: Anthropic is waiting until it can maintain consistent throughput before expanding distribution beyond initial Project Glasswing partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is waiting until it can 'reliably serve' Mythos to customers before expanding distribution. Rollout timing may depend on operational readiness rather than raw model availability.

key_facts.fact: Meanwhile, Opus 4.7 users are reporting the new tokenizer increases token consumption by about 30%, which burns through rate limits faster and raises costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 4.7 can also use up a whole lot more tokens. The model has a new tokenizer, which means that one input can cost significantly more.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic increased subscriber rate limits to compensate for the higher token burn, but critics on Reddit and X called Opus 4.7 a 'serious regression' in some use cases.
key_facts.excerpt: Cherny later announced that Anthropic was increasing 'subscriber rate limits to make up for it.' One Reddit post titled, 'Claude Opus 4.7 is a serious regression, not an upgrade,' has 2,300 upvotes.
